title: Tool Nomenclature Sanctifier and Runtime Call Fallbacks
creator: Avery Kim
description: Problem: customers and partner SDKs submit tool/function calls using a variety of name shapes (snake_case, camelCase, natural language labels, legacy numeric suffixes). This causes runtime routing failures, failed function invocations, and poor developer UX when the model refers to a tool by a name that does not exactly match the registered runtime entry. Goal: build a compact, deterministic runtime layer that canonicalizes tool names at call-time, preserves invocation provenance for auditing, and implements safe fallback policies to keep applications online while avoiding silent mis-invocations. This ticket covers design, runtime registry changes, API surface, tests, and rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a deterministic canonicalizer that maps incoming tool names to registered tool IDs with >99.9% success on our synthetic name-paraphrase corpus
Tool call path emits provenance headers (original_name, canonical_id, mapping_strategy) visible in logs and developer console
Fallback policy order implemented: exact match -> alias table -> normalized canonicalization -> semantic similarity lookup -> explicit failure
Streaming responses and function invocation boundaries are preserved (no token-level renaming mid-stream), and unit tests cover boundary cases
Feature gated rollout completed with metrics: mapping_rate, fallback_rate, invocation_misroute_incidents, and a dashboard created
Docs updated with migration guidance and examples for SDK callers and third-party tool registrars
proposal: We will implement a small name-normalization service inside the serving runtime that uses a lightweight, deterministic pipeline: (1) unicode normalization and trimming, (2) punctuation stripping, (3) tokenization + lowercasing, (4) alias table lookup, (5) canonical suffix/verb mapping (e.g., 'create-ticket' -> 'create_ticket'), and (6) optional semantic fallback using a compact embedding/ANN index for near-miss names. The alias table is editable via the console and persisted in the model catalog metadata. The runtime will attach a provenance header (X-RW-Tool-Orig, X-RW-Tool-Canonical, X-RW-Tool-Strategy) to each invocation record and forward those to logs and the console trace. To avoid silent errors, semantic fallback is opt-in per customer and rate-limited; by default it will surface a clear error with suggested candidates.
implementation_notes: Add canonicalization module to runtime/kernel pre-flight path; keep it <1ms median overhead by optimizing string ops and caching last-1000 mappings
Alias table stored in catalog service with a small in-memory LRU cache in each serving process
Expose new API fields in the call envelope: 'tool_hint' (client-provided), and return 'resolved_tool' in response metadata
Streaming consideration: resolved_tool must be computed and fixed before any 'tool_call' streaming frames are emitted; do not allow mid-stream renaming to avoid client confusion
Fallthrough semantic lookup implemented using quantized embeddings index (configurable per region) behind a feature flag
Add non-blocking metrics emission for mapping decisions to avoid impacting P95 latency
Audit log entries must include mapping_strategy and confidence score (if semantic lookup used)
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization pipeline with >100 synthetic permutations
Integration test with legacy SDK that submits 'OpenTicket-v1' and expects mapping to 'create_ticket' with provenance header
Load test measuring added latency at 1k QPS and verifying <2% P95 latency regression
Streaming smoke tests to verify token boundaries and no mid-stream renaming
Security review of provenance headers to ensure no sensitive data leakage
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood behind feature flag for 2 weeks (runtime-1.22-canary)
Phase 2: Opt-in customers enable semantic fallback; collect mapping metrics for 4 weeks
Phase 3: Gradual default enablement of deterministic canonicalization for all customers, disable semantic fallback by default
Phase 4: Console UI exposure for alias table editing and audit dashboard release
Rollback: feature flag + runtime config switch to disable canonicalizer and revert to exact-match behavior
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Catalog, and Console teams. Agreed on provenance header shape and alias table ownership.
2025-02-19: Prototype canonicalizer implemented in Rust shim; 95th percentile mapping latency ~0.4ms.
2025-02-25: Decided against always-on semantic fallback due to audit complexity; will be opt-in and rate-limited.
2025-03-01: Integration tests failing when streaming 'tool_call.start' emitted before name resolution; fixed by moving resolution earlier in the pipeline.
2025-03-06: WIP PR opened for in-memory LRU cache and dashboard metrics; requesting review from @sanjay and @elaine
notes_for_support: Support should watch 'mapping_rate' and 'fallback_rate' metrics during rollout. If customers report unexpected tool behavior, ask for invocation trace (trace id) to inspect X-RW-Tool-Orig and X-RW-Tool-Canonical headers.
